2 رزّم القَوْمُ , (K,) inf. n. تَرْزِيمٌ, (TA,) The people cast, or laid, themselves down upon the ground, (K, TA,) and remained fixed there, (TA,) not quitting their place. (K, TA.) ＝
-A2- رزّم الثِّيَابَ, (S, Msb, K,) inf. n. as above, (S, K,) He bound the clothes, or tied them up, (S, K,) in رِزَم [or bundles]: (S:) he made the clothes into رِزَم. (Msb.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
